name: Ammonia as marine fuel
principle: Ammonia burns in dual-fuel engines on ships. IEA reports that 4-stroke ammonia engines are commercially available for smaller vessels, 2-stroke engines for large ships are not yet commercial, and more than 30 ships are on order with deliveries from late 2025. IMO amended the IGC Code in December 2024 to permit ammonia cargo as a marine fuel, in force July 2026. IEA rates ammonia-fuelled ship engines at TRL 6.

performance.metric: ammonia as marine fuel - world-first operations and trials
performance.unit: tonnes of liquid ammonia used in the first bunker operation and 10-day propulsion/manoeuvrability trials (Fortescue Green Pioneer, Singapore, Mar-May 2024, with diesel and HVO)
performance.basis: Fortescue Green Pioneer carried out the world's first ammonia marine bunker operation in Singapore (announced 15 Mar 2024) and completed 10 days of trials (23 Apr - 2 May 2024) using 6.4 m3 (4.4 t) of liquid ammonia with diesel/HVO; MAN Energy Solutions ran the first ammonia test engine at its Copenhagen research centre in July 2023; Green Pioneer demonstrated in the UK from March 2025

source.note: Energy Connects, 15 Mar 2024; CleanTechnica 13 May 2024 (10-day trial, 6.4 m3/4.4 t); safety4sea 17 Jul 2023 (MAN first ammonia engine run); read 2026-10-28
